not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

## Owner's voice: one recording, every model (2026-10-15)

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

y**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

o**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

e**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

,**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

## Owner's voice: one recording, every model (2026-10-15)

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |

| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running

Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

m**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

9**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

l**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

.**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

w**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

n**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

e**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

|---|---|---|

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

-**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

r**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

E**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

-**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is

prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

r**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running

prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

## Owner's voice: one recording, every model (2026-10-15)

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

7**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

|---|---|---|

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

B**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

a**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

C**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

i**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

|---|---|---|

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,

prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

x**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

|---|---|---|

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

f**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

## Owner's voice: one recording, every model (2026-10-15)

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |

| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |

output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

m**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

 **`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording
was cut the way LARIS cuts it (`segment.py` replays the hands-free loop,
pre-roll included) and fed to each config. Plain turbo here matches what
LARIS pasted live.

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |
| turbo (LARIS today) | 11.3% | 31/42 | 0.12 s |
| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |
| Canary v2 | 25.2% | 21/42 | 0.08 s |

The prompt is the list in `scripts/stt_bench/bench.py:VOCABULARY_PROMPT`. It
holds the test's own terms, so 4.4% is what it does for words it lists,
not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

r**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.

The owner read the same 20 phrases again, with hands-free on (the spacing
and pre-roll fixes live) and `pw-record` keeping the audio. The recording

| config | WER | technical terms right | transcribe p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turbo + vocabulary prompt (list)** | **4.4%** | **40/42** | 0.12 s |
| turbo + vocabulary prompt (running text) | 5.7% | 36/42 | 0.13 s |

| large-v3 | 13.2% | 30/42 | 0.22 s |
| medium | 15.1% | 29/42 | 0.13 s |
| Parakeet v3 | 17.6% | 25/42 | 0.04 s |

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |

hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running

not for new ones. Terms it does not list (Kafka, Spring Boot, DeepFilterNet,
endpoint, GPU) came out right with and without it.

The price, measured on CORAA's 500 real pt-BR utterances:

| prompt | CORAA WER | utterances given project words nobody said |
|---|---|---|
| none | 20.3% | 0 |
| list | 21.2% | 9 (4 of them nothing but prompt words) |
| running text | 23.2% | 5 |

The leaks are on fillers and fragments: "aham" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,
MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "uh uh" -> "MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,". Without a
prompt, the same fragments already come out as "Obrigado." or "Tchau.". In
hands-free, a cough or an "aham" can paste the prompt's words. The running
text leaks less but loses on both sets.

**Model choice holds on the owner's voice:** turbo beats large-v3, medium,
Parakeet and Canary. Parakeet and Canary mangle English jargon ("Pai
Teste", "Fester Whisper", "Jason").

b**`INITIAL_PROMPT` is not a free fix.** The obvious lever for those misses is
LARIS's `INITIAL_PROMPT` (empty today). With the owner's vocabulary as the
prompt, turbo got worse on CORAA: 20.3 -> 21.2 WER overall and 40.9 -> 46.5
on 1-5 word utterances. On fragments and fillers the prompt leaks into the
output: "é" -> "LARIS, MIRIS, MIRIS, MIRIS,", "eh" -> "REST, JSON, venv.".
The next section measures it on the owner's own voice.
